what_its_for: Doxazosin is used to treat two conditions. First, it treats high blood pressure (hypertension) by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard. Second, it treats symptoms of an enlarged prostate gland (benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH) in men, helping to relax the muscles in the prostate and bladder so urine can flow more easily. This can reduce symptoms like difficulty starting urination, weak urine stream, and needing to urinate frequently or urgently.
how_to_take: Take doxazosin exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take the regular tablet (Cardura) with or without food. If you take the extended-release tablet (Cardura XL), take it with your morning meal. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or cut it. Try to take your medicine at the same time every day to help you remember. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to reduce side effects.
dosing: The starting dose is usually 1 mg once daily for regular tablets. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose up to 16 mg per day depending on how you respond to the medication. For the extended-release tablet (Cardura XL), the starting dose is usually 4 mg once daily with breakfast. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store doxazosin tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the medication away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Be very careful when standing up quickly from a sitting or lying position, especially when you first start taking this medicine or after a dose increase. Doxazosin can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure (called orthostatic hypotension), which may make you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or faint. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase the blood pressure-lowering effect and make dizziness worse. Avoid getting too hot or dehydrated, such as during exercise or in hot weather, as this can also lower your blood pressure further.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: sudden fainting or loss of consciousness, severe dizziness or feeling like you might pass out, chest pain or irregular heartbeat, a painful erection that will not go away (priapism — this is a medical emergency), swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: For high blood pressure, doxazosin starts working within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take several weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. For enlarged prostate symptoms, you may start to notice improvement in urinary symptoms within 1 to 2 weeks, but full benefit can take several more weeks. Keep taking this medicine even if you feel well, as high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering and dizziness effects of doxazosin. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and increase it slowly. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions to reduce your risk of falls. Kidney or liver problems: If you have liver disease, use this medicine with caution as your body may process it more slowly. Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or nursing. Children: Doxazosin is not approved for use in children.
